From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall:** The Seller's package moves toward or past our authorised fallbacks on almost every economic point. It also folds fraud, title, tax and IP into one general limitation regime. No fallback has been approved by Amelia Frost, so our response should restate the playbook's starting positions throughout.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000), clause 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket.** The Seller's figures are 5x our position, and the deductible structure permanently excludes the first AUD 250,000 of valid loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Clause 12.3/13 also applies "any limitation" to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the blanket "applies to all Claims" language.** 18 months is an unapproved fallback, and the default-application wording would silently extend the general limits to fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so capping them at 20% for 18 months is not an administrative point.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express overriding carve-out.** "Any nature" would on its face capture fraud. This position is non-waivable under the playbook, so it is not open to trade.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (as at 5.00pm 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only, meaning facts disclosed with enough detail to identify their nature and scope against particular warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; delete DL 1.1–1.2 general disclosures.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would gut the warranties. The specific disclosures in DL 2–10 can be assessed on their merits.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier should sit on the Seller side, limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete clause 8.3.** It combines constructive knowledge ("discoverable") with imputed adviser knowledge, which would neutralise the very matters we specifically diligenced, such as Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent. DL 2 confirms no final consent has been provided and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring an effective consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 and evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject consent-on-delivery and endeavours-only; make an effective consent plus satisfied conditions a hard CP.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), so a conditional or defective consent is a material customer risk.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, to be addressed by a release "following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-Completion release.** A deferred release is only acceptable with an irrevocable lender undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval, and we have neither. On a debt-free basis we should not take shares subject to change-control (cl 8.1) and undischarged security.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item or demonstrably Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require an express line item (or Treatment as Debt/Seller deduction) covering the bonuses and all on-costs, plus a specific indemnity.** These bonuses are payable by the Company on Completion, so "a matter for the Seller" with no mechanism leaves the cost with the Company we are buying.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity covering ownership, transfer and use of the SOW3 Project Materials, with the SOW3 cure preserved. That cure is evidence of cleared payment of every SOW3 fee plus a confirmatory assignment under DD-004 cl 7.3.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow wording; broaden the indemnity and add a pre-Completion deliverable of payment evidence and confirmatory assignment.** The risk is IP ownership, not just a fee. The AUD 180,000 figure (DD-010) is not independently verified either way, so the drafting should not assume it is paid or unpaid.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL 6 says access, scope and any notification duty are not established.
- **Buyer wants:** Covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and give the Buyer regular updates and consultation rights before Completion. Back these with a specific warranty or indemnity that does not presume an outcome.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation and add investigation/preservation/update covenants and specific protection.** On the current record there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss. Equally, the Seller's "not material" assertion is unsupported, so neither side should prejudge it.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total, DD-008/DD-011) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or genuinely ordinary course. DL 8 is silent on all of these.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet; request the contracts and timing and reserve the treatment.** We should not automatically classify the renewals as Debt or seek a price deduction. We need the facts first, especially because the renewals are related and should be read together.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single general regime governs everything. "Any limitation applies to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13), limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5), and tax/IP are treated as "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, specific payment items and covenant claims kept as separate categories, each with its own limitation terms, and no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; redraft so general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, with express exclusions for each other category.** The Seller's drafting collapses the categories through default wording rather than express negotiation.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 itself concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. This means an ASIC/PPSR search, a constitution check, share certificates, board and shareholder authority, and confirmation of no options, rights or security over the shares (cf. Riverlark).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient; require independent evidence as a Completion deliverable, backed by an uncapped title warranty.** DD-012 is an internal register supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain open and are to be negotiated separately. They are not resolved and are not assumed to carry unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation; respond that Tax/IP terms remain open.** Nothing has been agreed, and accepting this would import the 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k-deductible terms into Tax and IP by default.

---

### Other points from the Disclosure Letter
- **DL 1.4 (no admissions):** Acceptable as a general reservation, but it must not dilute the specific CPs and covenants above.
- **DL 7 (office lease) and DL 9 (Mossvale):** On the Seller's description, these involve a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not share-sale consents. We should verify this against DD-007 and DD-009 ourselves and add a covenant to give any required notices, rather than rely on the Seller's characterisation.

### Approvals flag
No point in this response should use a fallback position (the 20% cap, 18 months, or a post-Completion Riverlark release). If the deal team wants to move on any of these, we first need written authority from **Amelia Frost** that identifies this draft. The fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone.
